The most serious crime is second-degree murder (depraved-heart/extreme-recklessness murder). Firing a gun at a person in a crowded game shows a conscious disregard for an obvious risk to human life, so the killing is murder even without intent to kill. Transferred intent carries his intent to injure over to the teammate, but intent to wound alone is not premeditated intent to kill, so first-degree murder is unlikely. Felony murder is a weaker route that depends on the jurisdiction's list of predicate felonies and the merger doctrine.
